scenes.text: Why is South Asia one of the least integrated regions on Earth?
scenes.narration: Imagine living in a neighbourhood where neighbours almost never trade or talk. South Asia holds over 1.6 billion people, yet its intra-regional trade remains among the lowest on Earth!

scenes.text: A school group project where one angry member vetoes every single decision.
scenes.narration: Here is an everyday analogy: think of a school group project where every student has a veto. When two members fight, all decisions freeze, and no homework gets done!

scenes.heading: SAPTA Versus SAFTA
scenes.narration: Here is the trick: SAPTA failed because its positive list only allowed trade in rare items nobody bought. SAFTA aimed higher with a negative list, but political tensions stopped it.

scenes.heading: Why SAARC Stalled
items: India-Pakistan rivalry blocks all consensus decisions
Every member possesses absolute veto power
Countries lack a shared South Asian identity
scenes.narration: Why did SAARC collapse in practice? India and Pakistan represent 80% of the land and 90% of GDP, meaning their fierce rivalry and veto powers blocked every consensus.

scenes.heading: India Pivots to Sub-Regionalism
scenes.narration: When Pakistan vetoed the 2014 motor vehicle pact, India adapted quickly. New Delhi launched the BBIN sub-regional platform and pivoted its diplomatic energy towards BIMSTEC.

scenes.heading: The Revitalization of BIMSTEC

events.what: Founded as BIST by four nations
Nepal and Bhutan join the group
Leaders invited to Goa BRICS summit

scenes.narration: Look at how BIMSTEC stepped into the spotlight. Founded in 1997, it was revitalised after 2014 with a Dhaka secretariat, serving as a dynamic bridge to Southeast Asia.

items: Bilateral rivalry and consensus vetoes paralyzed SAARC
Sub-regional platforms like BBIN bypass regional blockades
BIMSTEC offers a high-growth bridge to Southeast Asia
scenes.narration: To wrap up: political rivalry and consensus vetoes paralyzed SAARC. India pivoted to sub-regional initiatives like BBIN, while BIMSTEC became a thriving, high-growth regional alternative.
